Abul Hashem ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Sheikh Ahmed and anr ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment: 4. Mr Ruhul Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the pre-emptor petitioner, submits that both the courts below on misinterpretation of section 92 of the Evidence Act and consideration of inadmissible extraneous evidence arrived at a concurrent finding that the deed in question dated 20-12-80 is not a deed of sale, rather a deed of release. The learned Advocate further submits that both the Courts below completely erred in fact that in view of Ext.2 there is no scope for the Courts below to consider any evidence which contradicts or tries to vary, add to or subtract the terms of the contract and from the recital of the deed in question it is crystal clear that it is a deed of sale and not the deed of release, as such, there was no scope for the pre-emptee opposite parties to lead any evidence to the contrary and both the Court below committed error of law in considering those evidence and arriving at a concurrent finding that the deed in question is not a deed of sale, rather it is a deed of release. Mr Ruhul Amen further submits that DW 1 admittedly was not present at the time of execution and registration of the kabala and none else supports him at the trial and except the evidence of DW 3 there is no other parol evidence to show that no consideration was passed from the pre-emptee to the executant of the deed in question. The learned Advocate further submits that it is the positive case of the pre-emptee opposite-parties that there was dispute amongst the heirs of Elahi Baksh and Haider Ali over a suit property and there was a ''salish'' held in the house of the Chairman but the Chairman was not examined in this case, rather DW 2 was examined who claimed to be the Chairman-in-charge and he proved the alleged ''salish''. The learned Advocate further submits that it is the positive case of the pre-emptee opposite-parties that the disputed deed is not a deed of sale but a deed of release. Yet they did not examine anyone of the attesting witnesses nor examined the scribe to substantiate their contention. The learned Advocate further submits that there is nothing on record to show that, in fact, there was a talk for execution and registration of a deed of release and not a deed of sale. The learned Advocate further submits that both the Courts below also committed an error in finding that the deed under pre-emption was a ''Nadabi'' deed. The learned Advocate further submits that after finding that the transferees were the heirs of Elahi Baksh, there can be no reasons for them to execute a Nadabi deed of no consideration and there can be no reasons for the heirs of Elahi Baksh to forego their interest in the land of Khatian No. 64. The learned Advocate further submits that merely because 10 other kabalas were executed and the inadequacy of the consideration of the kabalas under pre-emption is not a ground for holding that it was not a deed of sale but a deed of release. In support of his contention he refers to the following decisions, namely 39 DLR (AD) 78. 44 DLR (AD) 270,1983 BLD (AD) 105, 43 DLR 429, 35 DLR (AD) 334, PLD 1960 (Lahore) 231.
